title: Effective-resistance average trace identity and heat-kernel target
question: Can the tree-independent Gibbs-weighted effective-resistance average be rewritten exactly as the trace of the normalized Laplacian pseudoinverse, exposing an integrated heat-kernel target for the later uniform bound?
method: For every connected intrinsic graph, set D=diag(pi), W=D^(-1/2)L D^(-1/2), and u=sqrt(pi); enumerate the positive normalized spectrum above the declared numerical zero threshold.
Evaluate the unordered pair resistance average directly from L^+, the transformed pair sum from W^+, and the projector trace tr(W^+(I-u u^T)).
Check that all three quantities equal the positive inverse-spectrum sum sum_(k>0) lambda_k(W)^(-1) on the complete actual-likelihood grid.
Interpret the finite inverse-spectrum sum as the termwise integral int_0^infinity (Tr exp(-tW)-1) dt and retain the residual and positive-spectrum floor as conditioning inputs.
Use directed-pair doubling, unnormalized-L trace, one-mode-only and diagonal-q disconnected mutations as hostile controls.
finding: The primary lane passes 106990/106990 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 106990/106990; the hostile lane passes 6/6; the integrated verifier passes 37/37; and Lean R409 compiles. The resistance-average and normalized inverse-trace ranges are both [0.44413751605180657,2.0052069566897672]. The largest pair resistance is 85.99011817086347, the smallest positive normalized eigenvalue is 0.7570174175402339, and the maximum direct pair-to-trace residual is 2.537969834293108e-12; transformed-pair and projector residuals are at most 6.661338147750939e-16 and 4.440892098500626e-16.
decision_reason: This advances an exact finite Green/heat-trace interface: the future uniformity proof can target the total inverse normalized spectrum, equivalently an integrated heat trace, instead of a selected tree or only the smallest eigenvalue. The finite data do not establish a cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform trace bound, so no analytic gate is closed.

adversarial_review.check: Directed pair summation is exactly twice the unordered resistance average and is rejected against the trace identity.
The unnormalized-L inverse trace differs materially from the normalized trace on d=3 and d=12 representatives.
Keeping only the first positive inverse eigenvalue underestimates the full trace on both representatives.
Exactly d-1 positive modes are required above the declared numerical zero threshold; diagonal q gives zero edges and zero positive spectrum.
The non-importing lane rebuilds the finite oscillator, Gibbs, history, conditional graph and traces and agrees within 5e-6.
Finite trace equality does not prove a regulator-uniform Green bound, common core, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite resistance-trace and heat-kernel identity checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
next_action: Prove a cutoff- and volume-independent upper bound on the normalized Green trace or integrated heat trace on one Hamiltonian common core, control phase/source/orientation/exhaustion dependence, then transfer the resulting resistance inequality to the R-399 shell and combine with the R-406 Schur residual split. Stop or redesign if the trace diverges or the positive spectrum collapses.
no_overclaim: The trace identity changes the analytic target from a tree or a single eigenvalue to a total Green/heat-kernel quantity; it is not an analytic regulator, thermodynamic, physical-sector or QFT estimate.
